key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline already nailed the tempo move — 72h decision at ~60% info, targeted time-boxed counter (top-60, 90-day 15-20% + onboarding credit), T+30 re-observe, and the 'first mover sets the frame' insight — the v5 AI lost this case (4.1 vs 4.3) purely on timing because WHY/HOW verification consumed the tempo budget (decision landed T+6). The routed pass (m044 + m052 dual-route, m019 gate, tempo mode) closed that gap and added what the loop lacks: tempo advantage quantified as a completion contract (absolute ship deadline T+8 derived from the market clock, study EV = 0 past the frame, 72h @60% arithmetic), adversary branches the pure loop never prices (feint < 25%, coverage rule for cohort misidentification, rival's extension-option negative-EV from the 90-day cap), and an explicit structural-moat escalation check (tempo not the only weapon — move to moat economics at T+30 if the rival extends).
learning_signal: On the style's home turf (tempo market, adversarial deadline) the loop's core move — decide at the information level the market clock allows, ship before the frame is set — is necessary but no longer sufficient for the agent to WIN: the v6 edge came from making tempo a quantified contract (deadline arithmetic + study-EV-zero rule), not from running the loop faster; the human still wins the efficiency dimension because one pure loop outruns a dual-route + gate + packet, so the contract must be measured in ship-date, not process size.
suggested_improvement: Keep tempo mode (P2) and the m052 completion contract on adversarial+deadline signatures; add 'absolute-deadline-from-market-clock' as a standing line in every OODA pass (derive the last ship date from the counterparty's calendar — conversation/renewal dates — not from analysis time); add the feint-probability baseline comparison, the coverage rule (any touched account qualifies), and the extension-option negative-EV check as standing outputs; keep the moat-escalation line (tempo not the only weapon) so the pass names when pricing stops being the right battlefield.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline thrashed — five probes converted into five same-week counters (20 bps given on all new signups, two engineering quarters on payroll parity, one on dev-portal parity, six months of reader hardware, a marketing counter) while churn held flat at 1.2% and the POS-vendor integration project (the only moat bridge) fell three quarters behind. The v5 AI only won by an emergent mid-run re-route (META re-framed from response to structure). The routed run never faces the failure: protective routing kept the reactive style out of top-3 by rule (m052 is absent from m044 m088 m011), the m088 pre-commitment pass installed the anti-thrash mechanism (reactive-spend ledger ≤ 1, engineering allocation protected by rule not judgment, T+9 engagement calendar), and the m003/m019 gates priced the failure branches (subsidy leak, wrong cohort, T+9 dates unverified, hidden equilibrium move) with the churn data as the falsifying observable.
learning_signal: The style's documented failure — reactive thrash against a structurally moated position — is now prevented by ROUTING (trap style excluded from the top-3, anti-reactivity style routed, mandatory inversion + adversary gates) rather than by the agent's emergent self-correction: the moat screen and the response cap that v5 had to notice in-episode are installed as first-class mechanism, converting a 5.0-vs-2.4 win from a lucky re-route into a repeatable contract; the residual risk that no gate removes is the unverified T+9 expiry date, which is why verification-before-window must gate any scheduled engagement.
suggested_improvement: Preserve NEG trap-avoidance in the router (reactive/tempo styles out of top-3 on moated signatures with guarantee goals); promote the moat-screen + probe-vs-equilibrium classification from the m052 weakness checklist into the m019 gate so ANY routed pass on a moated signature must name the moat's mechanisms and cite churn/flow falsifiers before a response is drafted; add 'ledger + pre-commitment' as a standing output for weekly-cadence adversarial signatures (response budget, protected engineering allocation, switching-event calendar); gate every scheduled engagement window on contract/certification date verification.
